name: EngageBay
summary: All-in-one CRM, marketing, helpdesk and live chat for small teams — a genuine free tier (250 contacts) and per-user suites that undercut the big names.
best_for: small teams that want CRM, email marketing, helpdesk and live chat in one affordable suite — the free tier is a genuine trial-for-life, and it undercuts HubSpot hard at small scale
skip_if: your contact list is big (per-tier caps push you up fast) or you need best-of-breed depth in one area — all-in-one means good-at-everything, not best-at-anything
honest_knock: The meter is contacts AND seats at once: prices are per user, and each tier caps contacts — Basic’s 500 contacts fills fast, and the Growth jump is steep ($15 → $65 per user). The advertised ‘starts at $12.74’ assumes biennial prepay — two years upfront for the friendly number. Real automation only starts at Growth.

pricing.notes:
(price re-verified 2026-09-18 and again on 2026-10-05 on engagebay.com/pricing, which now redirects to /pricing/all-in-one) Genuinely free tier: $0 for 250 contacts with email marketing, CRM, helpdesk and live chat, and the plan card adds that it is free for teams of up to 15 members. All-in-One suite per user/month on monthly billing: Basic $14.99 (500 contacts), Growth $64.99 (5,000 contacts, marketing automation), Pro $119.99 (10,000 contacts). The three rates have not moved since our August reading, but the Pro contact allowance has: the plan card now says 10,000 contacts where we recorded 50,000. A note beside it confirms that ceiling in the vendor's own words — “The Pro plan includes up to 10,000 contacts” — and directs anyone who needs more to schedule a call about expanding the limit. The published ceiling is a fifth of what it was, and everything above it is now a sales conversation rather than a price.

Read the toggle before you read the number. The page defaults to a biennial ‘15% off’ display (Basic $12.74, Growth $55.24, Pro $101.99) with a yearly ‘8% off’ step in between ($13.79, $59.79, $110.39), so the friendly figure in the headline assumes you prepay two years. Single bays (Marketing or CRM & Sales) start at $11.04/user/mo on that same biennial display. One oddity worth knowing before you quote a number back to anyone: the page’s own title tag still advertises “Free to $99/Month”, and $99 is not a rate in any of the three billing columns.
